newsitem.title: FINLAND: OECD chief says South Korea better in than out.
newsitem.headline: OECD chief says South Korea better in than out.

text.p: South Korea is more likely to bring its labour legislation into line with international norms inside the OECD than it would on the outside, the OECD's chief Donald Johnston said on Monday.

"Is it not better to have Korea in the OECD -- being subject to peer review behind closed doors by all the members of the OECD ... than to have Korea outside the OECD?" the Secretary General told a news conference.

South Korea became the 29th member of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development in December, but provoked concern in the organisation with a labour crackdown after new labour laws were forced through parliament on December 26.
"What chance is there that the labour laws of Korea would have been reformed had Korea not joined the OECD?," Johnston said, after meeting representatives of Finnish industry here.

"There is no labour code in the OECD, but nonetheless -- because the OECD is a consensus organisation -- members will not accept a country unless it establishes criteria (and) those criteria can be in any area," he said.
"So it was ... quite understandable for concerns to be expressed with respect to the labour law," he said.
"The (labour) law that was adopted in December was seen as inadequate by many of the members," he said.

Korea's leaders had made commitments to meet some of the OECD's concerns and to put forward a new law, and had not backed away from pledges to move towards international labour standards, Johnston said.

"Some of the delays that have been built into that process have caused some concerns, but there were no actual periods stipulated by the OECD with respect to meeting some of those obligations," he said.
Its parliament on Monday passed a new bill, delaying for two years a clause that sparked worker fury by making it easier for companies to lay off staff.
